text:
Celerity is never more admired
Than by the negligent.
plain: Speed only impresses people who are slow.

text:
Well, I know not
What counts harsh Fortune casts upon my face,
But in my bosom shall she never come
To make my heart her vassal.
plain: Fortune can hit my face, but it never gets my heart.

text:
Who seeks, and will not take when once ’tis offered,
Shall never find it more.
plain: Hesitate when the chance is offered and it won't come twice.

text: If he do, sure he cannot weep ’t back again.
plain: You can't cry your fortune back once you've laughed it away.

text:
Be you not troubled with the time, which drives
O’er your content these strong necessities,
But let determined things to destiny
Hold unbewailed their way.
plain: Don't fret over what has to happen. Let it run its course.

text:
Fortune knows
We scorn her most when most she offers blows.
plain: The harder fate hits, the more you can laugh in its face.

text:
I see men’s judgments are
A parcel of their fortunes, and things outward
Do draw the inward quality after them
To suffer all alike.
plain: When luck turns, even your judgment goes with it.

text:
The loyalty well held to fools does make
Our faith mere folly. Yet he that can endure
To follow with allegiance a fallen lord
Does conquer him that did his master conquer,
And earns a place i’ th’ story.
plain: Staying loyal to someone who is falling is what earns a name.

text:
When valour preys on reason,
It eats the sword it fights with.
plain: Courage that kills your reasoning wrecks the weapon it fights with.

text:
There’s sap in’t yet. The next time I do fight
I’ll make Death love me, for I will contend
Even with his pestilent scythe.
plain: Still got sap in me. I'll make Death respect me.

text:
Never anger
Made good guard for itself.
plain: Anger never protected anybody.

text:
That which is now a horse, even with a thought
The rack dislimns and makes it indistinct
As water is in water.
plain: What looks solid dissolves as fast as a thought.

text:
Nay, good my fellows, do not please sharp fate
To grace it with your sorrows. Bid that welcome
Which comes to punish us, and we punish it,
Seeming to bear it lightly. Take me up.
plain: Take hard fate lightly and it loses some of its bite.

text:
Not Caesar’s valour hath o’erthrown Antony,
But Antony’s hath triumphed on itself.
plain: Nobody beat him but himself.

text:
Our size of sorrow,
Proportioned to our cause, must be as great
As that which makes it.
plain: Grief should be as big as what caused it. Don't shrink it for anyone.

text:
His legs bestrid the ocean; his reared arm
Crested the world; his voice was propertied
As all the tuned spheres, and that to friends;
But when he meant to quail and shake the orb,
He was as rattling thunder.
plain: Some people loom over the whole world, gentle with friends and thunder when crossed.

text: Make not your thoughts your prisons. No, dear queen;
plain: Don't turn your own thoughts into your prison.

text:
Sweet are the uses of adversity,
Which, like the toad, ugly and venomous,
Wears yet a precious jewel in his head;
And this our life, exempt from public haunt,
Finds tongues in trees, books in the running brooks,
Sermons in stones, and good in everything.
location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 1
plain: Hard times are teachers in disguise, and there's something good in everything.

text:
’Tis but an hour ago since it was nine,
And after one hour more ’twill be eleven.
And so from hour to hour we ripe and ripe,
And then from hour to hour we rot and rot,
And thereby hangs a tale.
location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 7
plain: Hour by hour we ripen, then we rot. That's all the story.

text:
All the world’s a stage,
And all the men and women merely players;
They have their exits and their entrances,
And one man in his time plays many parts,
His acts being seven ages.
location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 7
plain: Everyone plays many parts in a short run, then exits.

text:
Last scene of all,
That ends this strange eventful history,
Is second childishness and mere oblivion,
Sans teeth, sans eyes, sans taste, sans everything.
location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 7
plain: The last act is second childhood, then nothing.

text:
Thou seest we are not all alone unhappy.
This wide and universal theatre
Presents more woeful pageants than the scene
Wherein we play in.
location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 7
plain: Your pain isn't unique. The world is full of worse stages.

text: Love is merely a madness, and, I tell you, deserves as well a dark house and a whip as madmen do; and the reason why they are not so punished and cured is that the lunacy is so ordinary that the whippers are in love too.
location: As You Like It, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Love is madness, and nobody punishes it because everyone has it.

text: Time travels in divers paces with divers persons. I’ll tell you who time ambles withal, who time trots withal, who time gallops withal, and who he stands still withal.
location: As You Like It, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Time moves at a different speed for everyone.

text: The more pity that fools may not speak wisely what wise men do foolishly.
location: As You Like It, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: Fools get laughed at for the same things wise men do and call smart.

text: Nay, I shall ne’er be ware of mine own wit till I break my shins against it.
location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 4
plain: You don't see your own blind spot until you crash into it.

text: But as all is mortal in nature, so is all nature in love mortal in folly.
location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 4
plain: Everything natural dies, and everything in love goes foolish.

text: I will chide no breather in the world but myself, against whom I know most faults.
location: As You Like It, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Blame yourself first. You know your faults best.

text: I earn that I eat, get that I wear, owe no man hate, envy no man’s happiness, glad of other men’s good, content with my harm; and the greatest of my pride is to see my ewes graze and my lambs suck.
location: As You Like It, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Earn what you eat, envy no one, and be proud of simple work.

text: But all’s brave that youth mounts and folly guides. Who comes here?
location: As You Like It, Act 3 Scene 4
plain: Everything looks brave when youth rides and folly steers.

text:
Thou art not for the fashion of these times,
Where none will sweat but for promotion,
And having that do choke their service up
Even with the having. It is not so with thee.
location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 3
plain: Most people only work for the promotion, and the prize kills the effort.
